# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 17 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 17 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_017_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 17

**17:1** Now there went out a decree from the king Augustus that all those in Bethlehem of Judea should be enrolled. And Joseph said, "I will enroll my sons, but this child — what shall I do with her? How shall I enroll her? As my wife? I am ashamed. As my daughter? But the children of Israel know she is not my daughter. This day of the Lord will provide the answer for me as the Lord wills."

**17:2** And he saddled the donkey and set her on it, and his son led it and Joseph followed behind. And when they had drawn near to the third milestone, Joseph turned and saw her sad, and he said within himself, "Perhaps that which is within her is distressing her." And again Joseph turned and saw her laughing, and he said to her, "Mary, what ails you? One moment I see your face laughing and the next moment it is sad."

**17:3** And she said to Joseph, "Because I see two peoples with my eyes — the one weeping and lamenting, and the other rejoicing and exulting."

**17:4** And they came halfway on the road, and Mary said to him, "Take me down from the donkey, for that which is in me presses to come forth." And he took her down from there and said to her, "Where shall I take you and shelter you? For the place is desolate."
